title: Elodie and the Crown
premise: Juniper Crane, a bone-carver whose ledgers record debts owed by the living to the dead, has spent years hiding his gift inside the Guild of Impossible Things. When the border wards shatter, the stars extinguish, and a long winter begins to fall, Juniper learns that a soul he once carved a debt for—Elodie, the guildmaster's daughter, sold to the court beneath the mountain—is the keystone holding the wards together. To restore the sky, he must lead a ragtag found family of debtors and ghosts down into the under-court, where the Mountain King demands a price no ledger can balance: someone must stay in Elodie's place. Juniper offers himself, but Elodie refuses the rescue bought with his soul, and together they break the contract itself, freeing every soul the court holds and letting the wards be rebuilt on freely given memory rather than stolen life.
about_author: Coral Kavanagh is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate ledgers in a northern mill town before turning to fantasy. She writes stories about people who keep accounts—of money, of grief, of promises—and what it costs to forgive a debt.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Juniper Crane's POV. In the guildhall of the Guild of Impossible Things, Juniper carves bone talismans and records impossible trades, hiding his gift of hearing the dead from guildmaster Vess Crane and her daughter Elodie, who teases him into warmth. When a dying debtor's ghost begs him to 'count the stars before they go,' the emotional beat is the ache of a man pretending to be ordinary.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The border wards fail at moonrise and every star gutters dark; the dead's voices swell into a chorus of panic. Vess reveals the wards were anchored by a soul sold to the court beneath the mountain—Elodie's, sold at her birth. Juniper, who unknowingly notarized the sale years ago, is devastated; the beat is guilt crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Guild Owes
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie confronts her mother and learns she has been a walking collateral all her life. She decides to go under the mountain herself, and Juniper refuses to let her go alone. They recruit the guild's strangest debtors: a ghost-bound ferryman, a hedge-witch who trades in last words. The beat is fury transforming into fierce, chosen loyalty.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Toll
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The party crosses the drowned river at the world's edge, where the ferryman Bram demands a memory as toll. Juniper pays with his memory of his mother's voice, and Elodie quietly gives one of him instead, so he won't lose it. The beat is tenderness discovered mid-sacrifice, and the first hint that love is a debt neither wants to cancel.

chapters.title: Doors That Remember
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Descending through the under-mountain's bone corridors, the party passes doors that replay the memories of everyone who entered. Elodie sees her own christening, the moment of her sale, and her mother's grief. She begins to understand the Mountain King is not a monster but a bookkeeper, like Juniper—someone who confused accounting with mercy.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The party reaches the under-court, a hall of shelved souls glowing like lanterns, presided over by the Mountain King and his archivist, the pale thing that once bought Elodie. Juniper hears the dead here more clearly than ever—the shelved souls speak in unison. Negotiation begins; the King offers Elodie back for one soul of equal weight. The beat is dread dressed as diplomacy.

chapters.title: A Debt of Equal Weight
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper secretly offers his own soul, believing Elodie's life is worth more than his invisibility. Bram and the hedge-witch discover the bargain and, furious at being made into mourners, insist on sharing the price. The King, intrigued, sets a deadline: one soul or three by the final star's last light. The beat is love against duty, each trying to out-sacrifice the other.

chapters.title: Elodie Refuses
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie learns of Juniper's offer and rejects it—not from pride, but because she refuses a world rebuilt on someone else's stolen life. She studies the original contract with the archivist and finds the flaw: the wards run on consent that was never given. The beat is her claiming agency, turning from collateral into the story's true architect.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Contract
chapters.summary: Juniper and Elodie's interleaved POV. At the last star's dying light, they confront the Mountain King: Elodie formally refuses the sale, voiding the consent, while Juniper uses his bone-carving to rewrite the contract's terms, offering the court not souls but freely given memories from all the living above. The King, who only ever wanted to be remembered, accepts. The beat is the climax—audacity, terror, and grace.

chapters.title: Ledger Balanced
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The stars relight, the wards rise on consent and remembrance, and the shelved souls disperse—some to rest, some, like Bram's bound ghost, to finally go home. Vess asks Elodie's forgiveness; Elodie offers it as a gift, not a payment. Juniper and Elodie, no longer debtor and collateral, walk out of the guildhall into falling snow that is only weather. The beat is found family, and love chosen freely at last.
